screening.reason: Reports a diagnostic-prediction (ASD vs control classification) analysis of ABIDE I resting-state fMRI (ReHo) data, satisfying inclusion 2-3, despite being a short software/project report.

evidence_spans.text: The ABIDE dataset contains 539 individuals with ASD and 573 control subjects.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort used was the full ABIDE I preprocessed dataset: 539 ASD, 573 controls.

evidence_spans.text: First, participants were randomly divided into balanced split-half training and testing sets.
evidence_spans.claim: Evaluation used a single random balanced split-half train/test division, not cross-validation or leave-site-out.

evidence_spans.text: We specifically focused on the regional homogeneity (ReHo) fMRI derivative (Zang et al. 2004) from the Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (CPAC) pipeline (Craddock et al. 2013).
evidence_spans.claim: Feature was the ReHo derivative from the C-PAC pipeline (Preprocessed Connectomes Project release).

evidence_spans.text: The accuracy of our model without any dimensionality reduction or feature selection was ~ 62%.
evidence_spans.claim: Whole-brain voxel-wise ReHo SVM/logistic classifier achieved about 62% accuracy with no feature selection/dimensionality reduction.

evidence_spans.text: Using this program allowed us to build a sparse whole-brain biomarker that predicted diagnostic labels with 62% accuracy.
evidence_spans.claim: Main reported predictive result: 62% diagnostic accuracy.

evidence_spans.text: All data at ABIDE I Preprocessed are fully anonymized and hence are in compliance with HIPAA.
evidence_spans.claim: Used the ABIDE I Preprocessed (PCP) release, anonymized per HIPAA.

assessments.support: Full ABIDE I N (539/573) used with no stated QC/motion exclusion criteria described in the text.
ReHo voxel-wise features from C-PAC with no parcellation/atlas; no feature engineering beyond grey-matter masking.
Diagnosis labels taken as given from ABIDE without describing the diagnostic instrument in this report.

Single random balanced split-half train/test with no cross-validation, no confidence interval on the 62% accuracy, and no site-based or leave-site-out evaluation; this is a software demo rather than a validated biomarker study.

risk_of_bias.summary: A software/project report whose example use-case reports a single train/test split with no CV, no CI, and no site handling; demonstrative rather than a validated predictive model.

charting.title: Developing predictive imaging biomarkers using whole-brain classifiers: Application to the ABIDE I dataset
charting.gender_distribution: most subjects male, ratio of males/females identical in both groups
charting.new_dataset_contributed: no — contributes an open-source classification software tool
charting.dataset_openly_available: Uses the publicly available ABIDE I Preprocessed Connectomes Project release; no code repository link found in the text
charting.sensitive_data_anonymized: ABIDE I Preprocessed data are fully anonymized per HIPAA
charting.specific_features: Whole-brain grey-matter-masked voxel-wise ReHo (no parcellation/atlas, no feature reduction)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC pipeline (Preprocessed Connectomes Project, ABIDE I Preprocessed)
charting.specific_algorithms: Logistic regression-based classifier (prototype); SVM shown in Figure 1; scikit-learn implementation
charting.validation_methodology: Single random balanced split-half train/test split (no cross-validation used in the reported example)
charting.key_performance_results: ~62% accuracy without dimensionality reduction or feature selection
charting.summary_key_findings: A command-line, scikit-learn-based classifier tool was built and demonstrated on ABIDE I ReHo data, achieving ~62% accuracy for ASD-vs-control prediction on a single random split-half train/test division with no feature selection.
charting.future_directions_recommended: Feature selection/engineering and additional algorithms (random forest, Gaussian naive Bayes) to improve predictive accuracy
charting.reviewer_notes: Short Neurohackweek 2016 project/software report (5 pages); evaluation is a demonstration, not a validated biomarker claim.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction demo; ABIDE I Preprocessed (full release), n=539 ASD / 573 controls.
narrative_row.methods: Whole-brain grey-matter-masked voxel-wise ReHo features (C-PAC pipeline); scikit-learn logistic regression/SVM classifier; single random balanced split-half train/test division.
narrative_row.outcomes: ~62% classification accuracy without dimensionality reduction or feature selection.
narrative_row.key_limitations: No cross-validation, no confidence interval, no site handling, no stated QC/exclusion rule; authors themselves frame this as a software prototype/proof-of-concept rather than a validated biomarker.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A Neurohackweek software-tool report demonstrating a reusable open classifier pipeline on the full public ABIDE I Preprocessed release.
